Nearly 950 pounds of beef jerky recalled in Wisconsin and six other states over lack of federal inspection
 by Darren Siewert October 25, 2026 October 25, 2026 Share this:

 ( WASHINGTON ) Nearly 950 pounds of beef jerky distributed to stores in Wisconsin and six other Midwestern states are being recalled because the products were made without federal inspection and improperly displayed a USDA inspection mark.
 Imperio Distribution LLC, based in Elgin, Illinois, is recalling approximately 946 pounds of ready-to-eat beef jerky, according to an Oct. 24 announcement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).
 The products were packaged between January and October 2026 and sold at retail locations in Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota and Missouri.
 Which beef jerky products are recalled?
 The recall includes three varieties sold in 2-ounce sealed bags:
 Imperio Fuego Beef Jerky (Carne Seca) 
 Imperio Original Beef Jerky (Carne Seca) 
 Imperio Limón Beef Jerky (Carne Seca) 
 The recalled packages improperly display the USDA inspection mark bearing establishment number “1885,” which belongs to another facility.
 Consumers can view photos of the recalled product labels on the USDA website .
 Why is the beef jerky being recalled?
 Federal officials discovered the problem during routine FSIS surveillance activities.
 Because the beef jerky was produced without federal inspection, officials cannot verify that it meets federal food safety requirements.
 According to the USDA, food produced without inspection may contain undeclared allergens, harmful bacteria or other contaminants that could pose health risks.
 As of Oct. 24, no illnesses or injuries associated with the recalled products had been confirmed.
 What should consumers do?
 Federal officials are concerned that some of the recalled beef jerky may remain in consumers’ refrigerators or pantries or on store shelves.
 Consumers who purchased the affected products should not eat them. Instead, they should throw them away or return them to the store where they were purchased.
 The USDA is conducting recall effectiveness checks to ensure retailers have been notified and affected products are removed from sale.
 A list of retail locations that received the products may be published on the USDA recall website when available.
 Where to get more information
 Consumers with questions about the recall can contact Manuel Cortes, owner of Imperio Distribution LLC, at 630-532-9560 or [email protected] .
 Food safety questions can also be directed to the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-674-6854.
